construction.definition: In the normalization gamma=B=1, the source defines f_i(x)=(1/8)[delta_(i,1)(<x,v_0>^2-2a<x,v_0>)+sum_(r=1)^k delta_(i,r)(<x,v_(r-1)>-<x,v_r>)^2+delta_(i,k)<x,v_k>^2]. Directions v_0,...,v_k are orthonormal. At the end of round t, delta_(i,t)=1 for components not queried in that round and 0 for queried components; v_t is chosen orthogonal to earlier directions and previous query points. This is the printed construction; local corrections are separated below.
construction.hidden_objects: Orthonormal directions and component masks delta_(i,t).
construction.parameters: m>=2 integer; gamma,B>0; eta=epsilon/(gamma B^2) in (0,1/128). T=1/sqrt(32eta), k=floor(T)>=2, a=sqrt(3/(k+1)), q=floor(k/2), h=ceil(m/2), N=qh, d=N+k+2<=2mT. The source chooses a larger horizon-based dimension; this local repair gives an explicit sufficient dimension in the same assigned growing-dimension scope. General f_i(x)=gamma B^2 phi_i(x/B).
construction.public_information: m, gamma, B, dimension and component Oracle interface; directions and masks are hidden.

local_complete_argument.gap_and_integer_calibration: Every completed mask column has sum s, so with c=s/(8m) the eventual normalized average is F=G_(k+1), where G_t=c[z_0^2-2az_0+sum_(r=1)^(t-1)(z_(r-1)-z_r)^2+z_(t-1)^2] and a^2=3/(k+1). The preserved display repair proves min G_t=-ca^2*t/(t+1); the full minimizer has squared norm (2k+3)/(2k+4)<1. For a stop before N calls, all output coordinates z_r with r>=q vanish: if the incomplete round is t<=q, its future directions r>=t were chosen orthogonal to y. If t=1 all chain directions can be orthogonal to y. Thus F(y)=G_q(y), even for y outside the ball. Minimizing G_q over all its coordinates yields F(y)-min_X F >= ca^2[1/(q+1)-1/(k+2)]. Since s/m>=1/3, ca^2>=1/[8(k+1)]. Since q<=k/2, (k+1-q)/(q+1)>=1. The gap is at least 1/[8(k+1)(k+2)]>=1/(32k^2)>=eta, using (k+1)(k+2)<=4k^2 for every integer k>=2 and k<=T. Hence strict error below eta is impossible with n<N calls. Also floor(T)>=T/2 for T>2 and floor(k/2)>=k/3 for integers k>=2. Therefore N=hq>=mT/12=m/(12sqrt(32eta)). Finally h<=m, q<=k/2 and k+2<=2k imply d=N+k+2<=mk/2+2k<=3mk/2<=2mT for m>=2. This is the assigned O(m/sqrt(eta)) dimension and Omega(m/sqrt(eta)) call lower bound with explicit universal constants, including k=2 and odd m.
local_complete_argument.initialization_and_completion: Set T=1/sqrt(32eta), k=floor(T)>=2, q=floor(k/2), h=ceil(m/2), s=floor(m/2), N=qh and d=N+k+2. Work first at gamma=B=1. A round ends when h distinct indices have been queried; repeats also cost queries. During round 1 answer each query by the zero component Oracle: value and gradient zero, prox equal to projection onto the unit ball for beta>0, and zero for the minimum-norm beta=0 selection. At its completion assign delta_(i,1)=0 to its h queried indices and 1 to the s other indices. Choose v_0 and v_1 together, orthonormal and orthogonal to every query so far. This postponement is essential because the printed f_i^1 contains the not-yet-assigned delta_(i,1). During each subsequent round t, answer with the truncated polynomial f_i^t using only already fixed masks and directions. At round end set delta_(i,t)=0 for its queried indices and 1 otherwise, then choose v_t orthogonal to the earlier directions and all queries so far. Only rounds t<=q are needed. If the Algorithm stops after n<N calls, at most q-1 rounds have completed. Its arbitrary output y is now fixed by the deterministic transcript. For the current incomplete round assign exactly s ones among its unqueried indices (there are at least s+1 such indices), and zeros to all queried indices; assign exactly s ones in each subsequent mask column arbitrarily. Choose all remaining directions orthogonal to all n queries, y, and the already fixed directions; if no round completed, this includes v_0. No old mask or old direction is changed. If the Algorithm has not stopped, the adversary can run the transcript up to N-1 calls and complete an instance using the same rule with y=0 when no output has been produced; no early successful termination is possible. If j directions were fixed, the constraints have rank at most n+1+j and k+1-j further orthonormal directions are needed. The sufficient inequality d>=n+k+2 follows from d=N+k+2 and n<N. At ordinary round ends, without y, the count is smaller. Hence all choices exist. This construction is not a restriction on y or on queries; it chooses unrevealed directions after y is fixed.
local_complete_argument.model_membership_and_scaling: Let z_r=<x,v_r>. The component quadratic form Q_i(z)=delta_(i,1)z_0^2+sum_(r=1)^k delta_(i,r)(z_(r-1)-z_r)^2+delta_(i,k)z_k^2 is nonnegative and at most Q(z)=z_0^2+sum_(r=1)^k(z_(r-1)-z_r)^2+z_k^2. Using (a-b)^2<=2a^2+2b^2, Q(z)<=4sum_r z_r^2. Its matrix is positive semidefinite with operator norm at most 4. Since the component is (Q_i-2a delta_(i,1)z_0)/8, its Hessian is that matrix divided by 4, positive semidefinite and at most the identity. Components are therefore convex and 1-smooth on all R^d, hence on the ball. For general parameters use f_i(x)=gamma B^2 phi_i(x/B), where phi_i is the normalized component. Its Hessian is gamma times the normalized Hessian. Values, gradients and prox replies scale by gamma B^2, gamma B and B respectively, with normalized query x/B and normalized penalty beta/gamma. This follows by substituting u=Bw in the constrained prox objective and factoring gamma B^2. The beta=0 minimum-norm selection also respects this scaling. Error scales by gamma B^2 and call count and dimension are unchanged.
local_complete_argument.oracle_consistency: For a query made in round t>=2, eventual delta_(i,t)=0 and x has zero coordinates in v_t,...,v_k. The previously checked conditional projection proof at #/content/local_partial_repair/full_local_argument therefore gives equality of full and truncated values, gradients and constrained prox for beta>0. Every future direction is chosen orthogonal to this query. The full function splits into the known past polynomial plus a nonnegative future quadratic vanishing at zero. In round 1, queried components have delta_(i,1)=0, so they have no initial linear term and all their terms are nonnegative quadratics in directions orthogonal to the query. Projection onto the ball is a radial scaling of the query, annihilates these coordinates and minimizes distance over the ball; thus it also minimizes the full prox objective. Values and gradients are zero. For beta=0 define the Oracle once and for all to return the minimum-Euclidean-norm point in its component minimizer set. This set is nonempty, compact and convex on the ball; strict convexity of squared norm gives a unique selection. In the past/future decomposition, deleting future and chain-orthogonal coordinates preserves feasibility and never increases the component objective. Any minimum-norm minimizer must therefore have both coordinate blocks zero: otherwise its projection is a minimizer of smaller norm. The full and truncated minimum-norm minimizers consequently solve the same past-coordinate problem and agree. In round 1 that selection is zero. This fixes a valid deterministic beta=0 selection for the final fixed functions, not a history-dependent choice. The lower bound covers Algorithms allowed to request beta=0 against this valid Oracle; it does not assert that every possible tie-breaking rule hides the same information. Induction on the deterministic transcript now shows all simulated queries and responses coincide with one final fixed instance and fixed Oracle. Future rotations cannot change any earlier answer.

local_partial_repair.display_repairs: Set z_r=<x,v_r>, s=floor(m/2), c=s/(8m). After full mask completion, averaging gives F(x)=c[z_0^2-2az_0+sum_(r=1)^k(z_(r-1)-z_r)^2+z_k^2]. Define G_t=c[z_0^2-2az_0+sum_(r=1)^(t-1)(z_(r-1)-z_r)^2+z_(t-1)^2]. For 1<=t<=k this equals (1/m)sum_i[f_i^t+(delta_(i,t)/8)z_(t-1)^2]. Define G_(k+1)=F directly, without using delta_(i,k+1). On the first t chain coordinates, the quadratic form is positive definite: its energy is the sum of both endpoint squares and consecutive differences squared, which vanishes only when every coordinate vanishes. The stationary equations are 2z_0-z_1=a, 2z_r-z_(r-1)-z_(r+1)=0, and 2z_(t-1)-z_(t-2)=0, with the t=1 equation 2z_0=a. They give z_r=a(t-r)/(t+1), and substitution gives min G_t=-ca^2*t/(t+1). The minimum-norm optimizer has squared norm a^2*sum_(j=1)^t j^2/(t+1)^2=a^2*t*(2t+1)/(6(t+1))<=a^2*t/3. At a^2=3/(k+1), t=k+1 this is (2k+3)/(2k+4)<1. Thus feasibility holds with strict inequality. These are explicit local algebraic calculations, not a completed hardness proof.
local_partial_repair.full_local_argument: Write z_r=<u,v_r> and x=x_-+x_perp, where x_- belongs to span(v_0,...,v_(t-1)) and x_perp is orthogonal to every chain direction. Decompose u=u_-+u_++u_perp into the past, future and chain-orthogonal subspaces. Since delta_(i,t)=0, f_i(u)=g_i(u_-)+h_i(u_+), where g_i=f_i^t and h_i=(1/8)[sum_(r=t+1)^k delta_(i,r)(z_(r-1)-z_r)^2+delta_(i,k)z_k^2]>=0, with h_i(0)=0. The full prox objective is g_i(u_-)+h_i(u_+)+(beta/2)(||u_--x_-||^2+||u_+||^2+||u_perp-x_perp||^2). Replacing any feasible u by u_-+u_perp sets u_+=0, decreases its norm and therefore preserves ball feasibility. It cannot increase the objective, and for beta>0 strictly decreases it whenever u_+ is nonzero. The truncated objective omits h_i, so the same argument forces its minimizer to have u_+=0. On that feasible slice the two objectives coincide. Continuity and compactness give existence; convexity plus the positive quadratic penalty gives uniqueness. Hence their constrained prox points agree. This argument does not assert u_perp=x_perp and does not split the constrained minimization into independent problems. At a query with future coordinates zero, h_i and its gradient vanish, so values and gradients agree as well. Direct differentiation gives grad f_i^t(x)=(1/4)[delta_(i,1)(<x,v_0>-a)v_0+sum_(r=1)^(t-1) delta_(i,r)(<x,v_(r-1)>-<x,v_r>)(v_(r-1)-v_r)]. This proves conditional consistency only; adaptive initialization, output completion and calibration are separate.
